RagShortTexts: A deserter exposed Amida’s water passage in 359; infiltrators were later repelled.

Variants.Content: During the siege of Amida in 359, a miller familiar with the city deserted to the besiegers and identified a concealed water passage. Attackers used it to reach a high position inside before defenders repelled them. Everyday water and milling facilities became a weakness that local knowledge could exploit.

Defenders faced more than external engines: someone who knew a watercourse could reveal an internal approach. A miller’s local knowledge might exceed a distant officer’s view, without making all millers suspected traitors.

Urban authorities had to consider mills and waterworks alongside fortification. At Amida a deserter supplied the route, but the infiltrators were detected: intelligence, entry and occupation were separate achievements.
